reason: assigned single lap finished; not a handoff for context
did: state/laps.json was committed to main in dc27015 with unresolved git conflict markers. record-lap.mjs read it through a catch-all that returns an empty history for any parse failure, and --phase=start writes that back immediately — so the next lap to clone main would have erased eight samples plus the pending-verification record and committed it, while printing 'lap start recorded' and exiting 0. Parse failures now abort with exit 5; missing files still fall back.

observed_not_guessed.corruption_is_on_main_not_local: git show origin/main:state/laps.json throws at line 54 (position 1390). Markers at lines 54/61/68. Local HEAD 97db019 was clean, so this was only reachable by a fresh clone — which is how every automation runs.
observed_not_guessed.silent_erasure_reproduced: the old reader applied to the real origin/main blob returned samples: 0 and pending_verification: GONE. Two independent observations: direct JSON.parse throw, and the fallback's return value.
observed_not_guessed.guard_verified_end_to_end: with the corrupt blob in place, record-lap --phase=start exits 5 and leaves the file byte-identical (md5 before == after). With laps.json absent it still exits 0 and creates a fresh file, so a first-ever run is unaffected.
observed_not_guessed.test_catches_its_own_regression: mutation-tested: reverting parseStateFile to the swallowing behaviour makes tests/run-tests.mjs exit 1. Restored, it exits 0. A test asserting the committed laps.json parses would have caught dc27015 before it shipped.
observed_not_guessed.lap_cost_this_lap: not measurable — no_new_usage_reading (usage last collected 07:18:37Z, lap ran 07:52-07:59). Recorded as unusable, not as 0.

next_lap_should: The resolution problem the previous lap named is still open and is still the right next target, but check state/laps.json parses before trusting any of it. Two untried routes: (a) measure across several laps — one --phase=start, close after N fires — or (b) find a usage field finer than the 0.1%-rounded percentage. Note that route (a) now depends on the history surviving between laps, which is exactly what this lap fixed. Also worth 10 minutes: scripts/state-source.mjs readStateJson still returns { value: null, via: '... (unparseable)' } for a corrupt file, and every caller treats null as 'missing'. That is the same bug in a second place; it is non-destructive there (no write-back) but it silently blinds pacing.
known_gap: verify-sanitized-state.mjs checks for credential leaks but not for parseability, and no CI step parses the state/*.json files that Actions commits. A pre-commit or workflow assertion that every state/*.json parses would close the class, not just this instance.
